title: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
benefits: 5 kg of foodgrains (wheat/rice) per person per month completely free of cost to over 80 crore beneficiaries covered under NFSA.
eligibility_summary: All Priority Household (PHH) and Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) ration card holders.
details: The scheme "Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY)" has been launched by the Department of Food and Public Distribution, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India, and aims to ensure food security for the poor and vulnerable sections of the country by providing free food foodgrains. It was announced on 26 March 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic and is operated by the Department of Food and Public Distribution under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution. Through this scheme, free foodgrains (rice or wheat, depending on the State) are provided to eligible ration card holders covered under the National Food Security Act, 2013, namely Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households and Priority Households (PHH). From 1 January 2023, the scheme was integrated into the food security framework, and foodgrains earlier given at the highly subsidised rates of ₹1, ₹2, and ₹3 per kilogram for coarse cereals, wheat, and rice, respectively, are now provided free of cost. The scheme has been extended by the Union Cabinet for 5 years starting from 1 January 2024 and is approved for continuation till 31 December 2028, with a total financial outlay of ₹11.80 lakh crore (₹11,80,000 crore). The scheme is implemented through the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) by the state governments and Union Territory Administrations, with foodgrain allocation by the Government of India.
benefits_detailed: 1. Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) families receive 35 kilograms of foodgrains per family per month. 1. Priority Household (PHH) beneficiaries receive 5 kilograms of foodgrains per person per month. 1. The foodgrains are provided as rice or wheat, depending on the state, with fortified rice distributed nationwide. 1. Since January 2023, the foodgrains have been provided completely free of cost (at zero cost) to the beneficiaries. 1. Through One Nation One Ration Card, beneficiaries can collect their ration from any fair price shop anywhere in India.
eligibility_detailed: 1. The applicant should be a household belonging to the Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) category or the Priority Households (PHH) category. 1. Priority Households (PHH) are to be identified by the state governments/union territory administrations as per the criteria evolved by them. 1. Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) families are to be identified by the States / Union Territories as per the criteria prescribed by the Central Government, as listed below. > **Criteria for Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) Families:** 1. The applicant should be a household headed by a widow, a terminally ill person, a disabled person, or a person aged 60 years or more, with no assured means of subsistence or societal support. 1. The applicant should be a widow, a terminally ill person, a disabled person, a person aged 60 years or more, a single woman, or a single man, with no family or societal support, and with no assured means of subsistence. 1. The applicant should belong to a primitive tribal household. 1. The applicant should be a landless agricultural laborer, a marginal farmer, or a rural artisan or craftsman (such as a potter, tanner, weaver, blacksmith, or carpenter); a slum dweller; or a person earning a livelihood on a daily basis in the informal sector (such as a porter, coolie, rickshaw puller, handcart puller, fruit and flower seller, snake charmer, rag picker, cobbler, or destitute person); or a person in other similar categories in both rural and urban areas. 1. The applicant should belong to an eligible Below Poverty Line (BPL) family of a human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) positive person.

faqs.question: What is the scheme is about?
faqs.answer: It is a central government food security scheme implemented through the Public Distribution System (PDS), under which eligible ration card holders receive free rice or wheat every month, and it operates under the National Food Security Act (NFSA). It was announced on 26 March 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Families belonging to the Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) and Priority Households (PHH) categories, identified under the National Food Security Act, 2013, are eligible.

faqs.question: How much foodgrain will a beneficiary receive?
faqs.answer: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) families receive 35 kilograms of foodgrains per family per month, while Priority Household (PHH) beneficiaries receive 5 kilograms of foodgrains per person per month.

faqs.question: Do beneficiaries have to pay for the foodgrains?
faqs.answer: No. Since January 2023, the food grains have been provided completely free of cost (at zero cost) to the beneficiaries. Earlier, beneficiaries received their entitlement at the subsidized rates of ₹1, ₹2, and ₹3 per kilogram for coarse cereals, wheat, and rice, respectively.

faqs.question: Is there any application process for the scheme?
faqs.answer: No, there is no separate application process; the benefits are automatically provided to eligible National Food Security Act ration card holders.

faqs.question: What should an applicant do if they do not have a ration card?
faqs.answer: If the applicant does not already have a ration card under the National Food Security Act, the applicant should apply for one through the respective State Government's food and civil supplies department / portal; once the ration card is approved, the applicant automatically becomes eligible for the scheme. The issuance of Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) and Priority Household (PHH) ration cards is dealt with by the respective State Government / Union Territory Administration.

faqs.question: Can a beneficiary collect their ration from another State?
faqs.answer: Yes. Through One Nation One Ration Card, beneficiaries can collect their ration from any Fair Price Shop anywhere in India

faqs.question: What type of foodgrain is distributed?
faqs.answer: Rice or wheat is distributed depending on the State, with fortified rice distributed nationwide.

faqs.question: Till when is the scheme valid?
faqs.answer: The scheme has been extended by the Union Cabinet for 5 years starting from 1 January 2024, and is approved for continuation till 31 December 2028, with a total financial outlay of ₹11.80 lakh crore (₹11,80,000 crore).

faqs.question: What is the Mera Ration 2.0 application?
faqs.answer: Mera Ration 2.0 is a mobile application launched by the Department of Food and Public Distribution on 20 August 2024, which allows beneficiaries to check their monthly entitlement, view withdrawal history, and locate the nearest fair price shop.

title: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS)
ministry: Ministry of Rural Development
benefits: Monthly pension assistance (central component ₹200/month for age 60-79 and ₹500/month for age 80+, enhanced by matching state contributions up to ₹1,000–₹2,500/month).
eligibility_summary: Senior citizens aged 60 years or above living below the poverty line (BPL).
details: The scheme “Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS)” was started by the Department of Women &amp; Child Welfare, Govt. of Sikkim in 2014. Under this scheme, a pension is provided to elderly citizens above the age of 60 years belonging to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) category and the beneficiary will receive a monthly pension of ₹ 1500/-, ₹ 2000/- &amp; ₹ 2500/- as per eligibility criteria.
benefits_detailed: Monthly pension assistance (central component ₹200/month for age 60-79 and ₹500/month for age 80+, enhanced by matching state contributions up to ₹1,000–₹2,500/month).
eligibility_detailed:
- The applicant should be a resident of the state of Sikkim.
- The applicant should be from Below Poverty Line (BPL) family.
- The applicant should have attained the age of 60 years and above.
- The applicant should not have any source of income.
- The applicant should not be a recipient of salary/pension/family pension from Central Government / other State Governments.
- The applicant should have opened the Bank Account under “Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana”.
**Note 01:** In case both the husband &amp; wife are old age persons and are eligible for Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), only one member of the family shall be awarded the pension. In case of death of the pensioner, such pension shall be transferred to his/her spouse, if alive on surrender of the passbook, provided he/she has attained the age of 60 (sixty) years of age or more.
**Note 02:** Each beneficiary of the Pensions should submit &quot;Life Certificate&quot; in the prescribed format in the month of November every year failing which it will be presumed that the beneficiary is either died or migrated outside the State of Sikkim and the payment of pension shall be stopped forthwith without further notice.

faqs.answer: The IGNDPS is a component of the National Social Assistance Programme that provides monthly financial assistance to persons with severe or multiple disabilities belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) households.

faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development under the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP).

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply under IGNDPS?
faqs.answer: The person with severe or multiple disabilities must be aged 18 and above and belong to a Below Poverty Line (BPL) household as per government norms.

faqs.question: What is the benefit provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Eligible beneficiaries receive a monthly pension under the scheme. The central government provides financial assistance.

faqs.question: What type of disability is covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme covers persons with severe or multiple disabilities as defined under applicable government guidelines and disability certification norms.

faqs.question: Is a disability certificate mandatory for applying?
faqs.answer: Yes. The applicant must possess a valid disability certificate issued by a competent medical authority or medical board.

faqs.question: Can a beneficiary receive pension from another social welfare pension scheme simultaneously?
faqs.answer: No. Generally, a beneficiary receiving another social welfare pension is not eligible to receive benefits under the same category of pension schemes.

faqs.question: How can one apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Applicants can apply through the UMANG platform, NSAP portal, or through the concerned State/UT authorities and local bodies as prescribed by the respective state government.

faqs.question: When was the IGNDPS launched?
faqs.answer: The Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) was formally launched in February 2009 under the National Social Assistance Programme.

faqs.question: Is the scheme available in both rural and urban areas?
faqs.answer: Yes. The National Social Assistance Programme, including IGNDPS, is implemented in both rural and urban areas across India.

title: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
benefits: Free distribution of assisted living devices and physical aids: wheelchairs, walking sticks, hearing aids, crutches, artificial dentures, and spectacles to senior citizens.
eligibility_summary: Senior citizens aged 60+ belonging to BPL category or with monthly family income below ₹15,000 suffering from age-related disabilities.
details: The “Raah-Veer Yojana” was launched by the Home Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh. It aims to encourage the general public to help road accident victims during emergencies and save innocent lives during the critical Golden Hour by rewarding citizens who voluntarily take accident victims to a hospital for treatment. The scheme promotes civic responsibility and compassion among citizens by recognizing their bravery and humanitarian actions. > **Scheme Implementation** It is implemented by the Office of the Transport Commissioner, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, under the supervision of the State and District-Level Evaluation Committees and monitored by the Home Department.
benefits_detailed: **Tangible Benefits** - Provides a cash reward of ₹25,000 to individuals (“Rah-Veers”) who save the life of an accident victim by taking them to a hospital within the Golden Hour. - Selected “Rah-Veers” may be nominated for national-level awards by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH). - The MoRTH Evaluation Committee selects the top 10 Rah-Veers nationwide, each awarded ₹1,00,000, a certificate, and a trophy at the National Road Safety Mission (NRSM) in New Delhi. - Each individual can be awarded a maximum of 5 times per year under this scheme. **Mode of Disbursement** - The payment is made online directly to the beneficiary’s bank account through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). **Frequency of Disbursement** - One-time per eligible instance, up to a maximum of 5 instances per year. **Expected Time of Disbursement** - The payment is processed within 1 month after the District Evaluation Committee’s approval.
eligibility_detailed: 1. The applicant should be a resident of Madhya Pradesh. 1. The applicant should be any individual (citizen or resident) who voluntarily assists a road accident victim in a motor vehicle-related accident. 1. The applicant must have helped the victim reach a hospital within the Golden Hour, ensuring the victim’s survival.

If the Rah-Veer takes the victim directly to the hospital, the hospital must inform the local police station.
The police then issue the acknowledgment slip as above.

Conducts quarterly reviews to ensure smooth implementation.
After approval, the Transport Commissioner, Bhopal, processes the payment directly into the Rah-Veer’s bank account through PFMS.
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) provides monthly reimbursement to the State Transport Department.
Each year, up to three exceptional Rah-Veers are nominated for national awards.

title: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY)
ministry: Ministry of Finance
benefits: Government-backed savings account for girl children with an attractive 8.2% annual interest rate, exempt under 80C, partial withdrawal at age 18 for higher education.
eligibility_summary: Parents or legal guardians can open an account for any girl child up to 10 years of age (maximum two girl children per family).
details:
**Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY)** is an official flagship initiative administered by the **Ministry of Finance** aimed at uplifting eligible citizens across the nation.

The scheme was established under the **Women & Child** portfolio to provide direct financial assistance, socio-economic empowerment, and institutional welfare support to target beneficiaries. Eligible applicants are facilitated with direct benefit transfers (DBT), subsidy components, or protective social security benefits following transparent verification guidelines established by the government.

Under current operating directives, the scheme serves to enhance accessibility for Parents or legal guardians can open an account for any girl child up to 10 years of age (maximum two girl children per family). and ensures equitable distribution of government assistance through digital and transparent public service delivery channels.
benefits_detailed:
### Key Benefits & Entitlements

* **Core Financial / Welfare Support:** Government-backed savings account for girl children with an attractive 8.2% annual interest rate, exempt under 80C, partial withdrawal at age 18 for higher education.
* **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT):** Financial assistance and subsidies are deposited directly into the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank account (BSBDA / Jan Dhan compatible).
* **Institutional Safeguards:** Complete waiver of hidden processing charges or intermediary fees; state/central monitoring ensures timely disbursement.
* **Complementary Services:** Eligible beneficiaries may also access associated capacity-building, health cover, or subsidized credit support under allied government programs.
eligibility_detailed:
### Eligibility Requirements

1. **Residency & Domicile:** The applicant must be a citizen of India.
2. **Age Bracket:** Standard adult Indian citizen age guidelines apply.
3. **Target Beneficiary Profile:** Parents or legal guardians can open an account for any girl child up to 10 years of age (maximum two girl children per family).
4. **Gender Eligibility:** Open to **Female** applicants.
5. **Income Criterion:** Eligible income categories include: Below ₹1,00,000 per annum, ₹1,00,000 to ₹2,50,000 per annum, ₹2,50,000 to ₹5,00,000 per annum, ₹5,00,000 to ₹8,00,000 per annum, ₹8,00,000 to ₹10,00,000 per annum, Above ₹10,00,000 per annum.
6. **Social Categories:** GENERAL, SC, ST, OBC communities.
7. **Applicable Occupations:** Student, Unemployed.
8. **Geographical Coverage:** Beneficiaries residing in Urban and Rural areas.

> **Exclusion Criteria:** Individuals already drawing duplicate central/state pensions under identical heads, or taxpayers filing annual income above designated threshold brackets may be disqualified as per official guidelines.

faqs.answer: No, the Government does not charge any application or registration fee for this welfare scheme. Citizens are cautioned against paying any unauthorized agents or intermediaries.

title: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana 2.0 (PMUY)
ministry: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
benefits: Free LPG gas connection with deposit-free cylinder, pressure regulator, safety hose, first refill and hotplate stove completely free, plus ₹300 per cylinder subsidy on ongoing refills.
eligibility_summary: Adult woman belonging to poor households (SC/ST, PMAY beneficiaries, AAY, tea garden workers, forest dwellers, or verified under 14-point SECC declaration).
documents: Aadhaar Card of applicant & family members
details:
In May 2016, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MOPNG), introduced the ‘Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana’ (PMUY) as a flagship scheme with an objective to make clean cooking fuel such as LPG available to the rural and deprived households which were otherwise using traditional cooking fuels such as firewood, coal, cow-dung cakes etc. Usage of traditional cooking fuels had detrimental impacts on the health of rural women as well as on the environment.
The scheme was launched on 1st May 2016 in Ballia, Uttar Pradesh by Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Shri. Narendra Modi


- The target under the scheme was to release 8 Crore LPG Connections to the deprived households by March 2020.
- On 7th September 2019, Hon’ble Prime Minister of India handed over the 8th Crore LPG connection in Aurangabad, Maharashtra.
- The release of 8 Crore LPG connections under the scheme has also helped in increasing the LPG coverage from 62% on 1st May 2016 to 99.8% as on 1st April 2021.
- Under the Union Budget for FY 21-22, provision for release of additional 1 Crore LPG connections under the PMUY scheme has been made. In this phase, special facility has been given to migrant families.

title: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)
ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
benefits: Multi-sectoral intervention ensuring protection, survival, education, and equal inheritance rights for girl children, elimination of sex-selection, and subsidized schooling.
eligibility_summary: All girl children and their parents across all districts in India.
details:
**Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)** is an official flagship initiative administered by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development** aimed at uplifting eligible citizens across the nation.

The scheme was established under the **Women & Child** portfolio to provide direct financial assistance, socio-economic empowerment, and institutional welfare support to target beneficiaries. Eligible applicants are facilitated with direct benefit transfers (DBT), subsidy components, or protective social security benefits following transparent verification guidelines established by the government.

Under current operating directives, the scheme serves to enhance accessibility for All girl children and their parents across all districts in India. and ensures equitable distribution of government assistance through digital and transparent public service delivery channels.
benefits_detailed:
### Key Benefits & Entitlements

* **Core Financial / Welfare Support:** Multi-sectoral intervention ensuring protection, survival, education, and equal inheritance rights for girl children, elimination of sex-selection, and subsidized schooling.
* **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT):** Financial assistance and subsidies are deposited directly into the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank account (BSBDA / Jan Dhan compatible).
* **Institutional Safeguards:** Complete waiver of hidden processing charges or intermediary fees; state/central monitoring ensures timely disbursement.
* **Complementary Services:** Eligible beneficiaries may also access associated capacity-building, health cover, or subsidized credit support under allied government programs.
eligibility_detailed:
### Eligibility Requirements

1. **Residency & Domicile:** The applicant must be a citizen of India.
2. **Age Bracket:** Standard adult Indian citizen age guidelines apply.
3. **Target Beneficiary Profile:** All girl children and their parents across all districts in India.
4. **Gender Eligibility:** Open to **Female** applicants.
5. **Income Criterion:** Eligible income categories include: Below ₹1,00,000 per annum, ₹1,00,000 to ₹2,50,000 per annum, ₹2,50,000 to ₹5,00,000 per annum, ₹5,00,000 to ₹8,00,000 per annum, ₹8,00,000 to ₹10,00,000 per annum, Above ₹10,00,000 per annum.
6. **Social Categories:** GENERAL, SC, ST, OBC communities.
7. **Applicable Occupations:** Student, Unemployed.
8. **Geographical Coverage:** Beneficiaries residing in Urban and Rural areas.

> **Exclusion Criteria:** Individuals already drawing duplicate central/state pensions under identical heads, or taxpayers filing annual income above designated threshold brackets may be disqualified as per official guidelines.

steps.title: Access Official Portal
steps.description: Navigate to the official scheme portal at https://wcd.nic.in/bbbp-schemes or the state single-window citizen welfare portal.

steps.title: Citizen Registration & Aadhaar e-KYC
steps.description: Click on 'Apply Online / New Registration', provide your active mobile number, and complete Aadhaar OTP verification.

steps.title: Complete Application Form
steps.description: Fill in your demographic profile, family details, bank account credentials (IFSC code, Account number), and select 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)'.

steps.title: Upload Required Documents
steps.description: Upload scanned copies of required documents (Aadhaar, income certificate, bank passbook) in PDF/JPEG format (typically under 2MB).

steps.title: Submit & Save Acknowledgement
steps.description: Review your submitted information, click Final Submit, and save or print the Application Acknowledgement Number for tracking.

steps.title: Obtain Application Form
steps.description: Collect the official application form free of cost from the nearest Gram Panchayat office, Block Development Office (BDO), Municipal Ward office, or Common Service Centre (CSC).

steps.title: Attach Self-Attested Documents
steps.description: Fill the form in legible handwriting and attach self-attested photocopies of Aadhaar, bank passbook, domicile, and passport size photographs.

steps.title: Submit & Collect Receipt
steps.description: Submit the completed application dossier to the designated Nodal Officer or CSC desk and obtain a dated, stamped acknowledgment receipt.

faqs.question: What is the primary objective of Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)?
faqs.answer: The primary objective is to provide structured financial support, social security, and welfare assistance to eligible beneficiaries under the supervision of Ministry of Women and Child Development.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Eligibility is determined by age, residency, income bracket, and category. In brief: All girl children and their parents across all districts in India.

faqs.question: Is there any application fee required to apply?
faqs.answer: No, the Government does not charge any application or registration fee for this welfare scheme. Citizens are cautioned against paying any unauthorized agents or intermediaries.

faqs.question: How are the benefits or funds disbursed to the beneficiary?
faqs.answer: All financial benefits are disbursed via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into the applicant's bank account linked with Aadhaar, eliminating middlemen and ensuring prompt delivery.

faqs.question: Where can I track my submitted application status?
faqs.answer: You can track application status online using your application acknowledgment number on the official portal (https://wcd.nic.in/bbbp-schemes) or by visiting your local Block Development / CSC office.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the “Working Women Hostel” scheme?

faqs.question: Which department is responsible for implementing the “Working Women Hostel” scheme in Haryana?
faqs.answer: The Women and Child Development Department, Government of Haryana, is responsible for the implementation and overall supervision of the “Working Women Hostel” scheme across various designated locations in the state.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply under the “Working Women Hostel” scheme?
faqs.answer: Any woman who is currently working and requires accommodation due to employment away from her native residence is eligible to apply under the “Working Women Hostel” scheme.

faqs.question: What are the rent charges applicable to beneficiaries staying in hostels under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Under the “Working Women Hostel” scheme, the rent charged from beneficiaries is subsidized and varies depending on the type of room; it is limited to 15% of gross salary for single bedrooms, 10% for double bedrooms, and 7.5% for dormitory accommodation.

faqs.question: Are there any income limits or salary caps for availing hostel accommodation?
faqs.answer: Although the scheme does not specify a strict income cap, the rent charged is proportionate to the applicant’s salary, thereby making the accommodation affordable for working women across different income brackets.

faqs.question: What is the process for applying to the "Working Women Hostel" scheme?
faqs.answer: The applicants may visit the [Antyodaya-SARAL Portal](https://saralharyana.gov.in/) to apply for the scheme.

faqs.question: What is the offline process for applying the scheme?
faqs.answer: To apply for the "Working Women Hostel" scheme, the applicant may visit the nearest Atal Seva Kendra (Common Service Centre).

faqs.question: Is there any fee applicable for applying under this scheme through Atal Seva Kendra (Common Service Centre)?
faqs.answer: Yes, a nominal service fee of ₹10/- is charged by the Common Service Centre for the application.

faqs.question: Are there any specific documents that need to be submitted with the application form?
faqs.answer: Yes, applicants are required to submit several documents, including the Parivar Pehchan Patra Number, visitor list, local guardian appointment and acceptance, medical certificate, undertaking, character certificate, and a financial guarantee.

faqs.question: Does the scheme provide hostel facilities in all districts of Haryana?
faqs.answer: Yes, hostel facilities under the “Working Women Hostel” scheme is provided in all districts of Haryana.

faqs.question: What are the advantages of Grid-Connected Rooftop Solar System?
faqs.answer:
Saving on electricity bill by the consumer.
Utilization of available vacant roof space, no additional land required.
Low gestation period.
No additional requirement of transmission and distribution (T&D) lines.
Reduces T&D losses as power consumption and generation are collocated.
Improvement in the tail-end grid voltages and reduction of system congestion.
Long term energy and ecological security by reduction in carbon emission.
Better management of daytime peak loads by DISCOM/ utility.
Meeting of the Renewable Purchase Obligations (RPOs) of obligated entities

the roof for solar rooftop installation from the owner, he/she can install the RTS.

title: Jal Jeevan Mission (Har Ghar Nal Se Jal)
ministry: Ministry of Jal Shakti
benefits: Providing functional household tap connections (FHTC) with assured supply of 55 litres of safe potable water per capita per day to every rural household.
eligibility_summary: All rural households across all villages and habitations in India.
benefits_detailed: Providing functional household tap connections (FHTC) with assured supply of 55 litres of safe potable water per capita per day to every rural household.
eligibility_detailed: This scheme is applicable to all households in rural India.

children.text: The applicant need not apply for the scheme.

State Governments/ UT Administration will implement the mission based on the finalized SAP with timelines to cover all the villages of the respective State/ UT. Each village will be assessed on existing water supply infrastructure by DWSM in consultation with Gram Panchayat and/ or its sub-committee and ISA. Based on the same, FHTCs will be provided to every rural household by creating in-village water supply infrastructure including source development under any one of the following suggested categories, viz.
Retrofitting of ongoing schemes taken up under erstwhile NRDWP for the last mile connectivity;
Retrofitting of completed rural water supply schemes to make it JJM compliant;
Single Village Scheme (SVS) in villages having adequate groundwater/ spring water/ local or surface water source of prescribed quality;
Single Village Scheme (SVS) in villages having adequate groundwater that needs treatment;
Multi Village Scheme (MVS) with water grids/ regional water supply scheme; and
Mini solar power-based piped water supply in isolated/ tribal hamlets.

documents_required: Any proof of identity like Voter ID / Passport / Driving License / Ration Card / Aadhaar Card etc. is sufficient to apply for water connection

faqs.question: How water will be provided to households where tap water connections are not feasible?
faqs.answer:
In such areas, local innovations/ technological solutions will be explored. Suggestive technological solutions to address challenges in the supply of drinking water are as under:

Solar energy based stand-alone water supply systems for scattered/ isolated/ tribal/ hilly villages.
Community Water Purification Plant (CWPP) in groundwater contaminated areas.
In cold deserts, solutions may be explored to enhance and store run-off water in small tanks - traditional water harvesting structure, i.e. Zings of Ladakh. Further, artificial glacial reservoirs may be created by diverting the run-off to freeze & store as glacier.
In hard rock areas, bore-blast technique, fracture seal cementation, stream blasting, etc. may be explored.
In hilly areas, adopting spring-based sources, rain water harvesting and standalone bore-well systems (if feasible) will be explored.
In coastal areas, energy efficient small desalination plants with high recovery ratio will be explored, along with construction of sub-surface dykes in rivers.
Use of Internet of Things (IoT), Geographic Information System (GIS) software, etc., will be required for planning and monitoring.

title: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)
ministry: Ministry of Rural Development
benefits: Connecting eligible unconnected rural habitations (population 500+ in plain areas and 250+ in hill states) with all-weather blacktopped roads.
eligibility_summary: Rural habitations currently lacking all-weather connectivity.
details:
With the objective of providing rural connectivity, the Government of India launched the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (referred to as PMGSY-I hereinafter) on 25th December 2000 to provide all-weather access to eligible unconnected habitations with a population of up to 500(Census 2001) in plain area and 250 and above in Special category States(States of North East, Jammu, and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand), Desert Area as identified by Desert Development Program and 88 selected Backward Districts as identified by the Ministry of Home Affairs/Planning Commission as a strategy for poverty alleviation.
As of 8th December 2021, a total of 6,80,040 km of road length has been constructed under various interventions of Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY). The primary objective of PMGSY concerns building robust, all-weather roads in rural habitations and other core areas. Panchayati Rajs and elected local representatives decide which habitations to be selected. This scheme was centrally funded only up to 2015-16. Since then, the funds have been divided between the Centre and the State. For North Eastern and Himalayan States (Jammu & Kashmir, Uttarakhand, and Himachal Pradesh) 90% of a project is the Union Government funds, and 10% of this cost, is the State Government funds. For the Other States, the Union Government funds around 60% of a project while the remaining 40% is by State Government funds.
Some prominent features of PMGSY are - Proper decentralized planning for the building of roads. Build roads according to the Indian Road Congress and Rural Roads Manual. 3-tier quality management system. An unbroken flow of funds.
benefits_detailed: Connecting eligible unconnected rural habitations (population 500+ in plain areas and 250+ in hill states) with all-weather blacktopped roads.
eligibility_detailed:
1. A region must be a habitation. It cannot be a hamlet or revenue village to be eligible for the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY).
2. The Central Government describes habitation as a population cluster residing within an area that remains constant over time. Some of the local words used to describe a habitation are: Majras, Desam, Hamlets, Tolas, Dhanis
3. The hamlet must have a higher population as per the 2001 Census to be eligible for road connection. The eligible habitations have a population of above 500 persons in plain areas and around 250 persons and above in hilly areas.

children.text: The list of road works to be taken up under the Programme will be finalized each year by the District Panchayat in accordance with the allocation of funds communicated to the district. The District Panchayat has to ensure along with the consultative process, that the lists of proposed road works are part of the Core Network and that new connectivity is given priority.

documents_required: The release of the second installment in a year shall be subject to the submission of the following documents:
1.  Utilisation Certificate for the funds released earlier, year-wise in the form prescribed.
2.  Certificate by the Bank Manager indicating the balance amount on the date of issue of the Certificate and the interest credited.
3.  A Certificate regarding the requisite physical completion of works

4.  For all releases after October of a year, production of an Audited Statement of Accounts and a Balance Sheet and related Statements, duly certified by the Chartered Accountant for the accounts of the previous financial year.
5.  Outputs of the relevant modules of the OMMAS, duly certified by the SRRDA as being correct and verified by the NRIDA

6.  A certificate from the CEO of SRRDA that Maintenance funds required as per maintenance contracts in force had been spent during the previous financial year. For releases after May of a year, the certificate should also include that 50% of such maintenance fund requirements for the current Financial Year have been released by the State, whereas for releases after November, the certificate should be for 100% of such funds.

faqs.question: Does The Programme Provide Connectivity To Only Revenue Villages? Are Hamlets Eligible To Be Connected?
faqs.answer:
The spirit and objective of PMGSY-I was to provide good all-weather road connectivity to eligible unconnected habitations. The unit of this programme is a habitation and not a revenue village or a Panchayat. A habitation is a cluster of population, living in an area, the location of which does not change over time. Desam, Dhanis, Tolas, Majras, Hamlets, etc. are commonly used to describe habitations.

The population, as recorded in the Census 2001, shall be the basis for determining the population size of the habitation. The population of all Habitations within a radius of 500 metre (1.5 km of path distance in case of Hills) may be clubbed together to determine the population size. In the blocks bordering international boundary in the hill States (as identified by the Ministry of Home Affairs), however, all habitations within a path distance of 10 km may be treated as a cluster for this purpose. This cluster approach would enable the provision of connectivity to a number of Habitations, particularly in Hill/ mountainous areas.

A special dispensation has been allowed to Arunachal Pradesh under PMGSY by extending the Cluster approach to all International border districts in the State by clubbing population with the path distance of 10 km and treating as a Cluster.

faqs.question: How Are Habitations Selected For Coverage? Who Decides Which Habitations Will Be Covered In A Year?
faqs.answer: Unconnected habitations are listed as per the priority (generally, habitations with a higher population, as per 2001 Census, would be connected first) and depending upon the funds likely to be made available for the State, the list of road works to be taken up under PMGSY-I will be finalized each year by the District Panchayat through a consultative process involving Panchayati Raj Institutions and elected representatives.

faqs.question: Can An Individual Apply For Road Connectivity?
faqs.answer: The objective of PMGSY-I was to provide road connectivity to unconnected habitations as mentioned in response to Question 1 above. Any proposal for road connectivity may be perceived as per the programme guidelines.

faqs.question: How Is Alignment Selected? Are Local Villagers Associated With This Process?
faqs.answer: A simple, non-formal transect walk shall be organised by the Assistant Engineer at the time of preparation of DPRs to finalise the alignment. The Panchayat Pradhan, local patwari, the JE, Local Revenue and Forest officials, Women PRI members and representatives of Women Self Help Groups (SHGs) also participate in the transect walk to determine the most suitable alignment, sort out the issues of land availability and to moderate any adverse social and environmental impact, eliciting necessary community participation in the programme. After transect walk, the minutes should be placed and approved by the Grama Sabha.Local people including those likely to be affected by proposed alignment are also allowed to put forth their view in this process.

faqs.question: What Does All-Weather Connectivity Mean? Does It Mean Only Black- Topped Or Cement Concrete Roads?
faqs.answer: An all-weather road is one that is negotiable in all seasons of the year. This implies that the road-bed is drained effectively but this does not necessarily imply that it should be paved surface with blacktopping or cement concrete. A gravel road can also be an all-weather road.

faqs.question: How Is The Problem Of Drainage Tackled In The Portion Of Roads Passing Through Built-Up Residential Areas?
faqs.answer: Road portions passing through built-up residential areas are prone to damages caused by wastewater from households. Programme guidelines provide for the construction of cement concrete pavement or cement/stone block pavements along with covered or uncovered Pucca side drains as per site conditions.

faqs.question: Is The Adequate Provision For Culverts Or Cross-Drainage Works Made?
faqs.answer:
The objective of the PMGSY is to provide an All-weather Road with necessary culverts and other cross drainage structures, which is operable throughout the year to the eligible unconnected habitations as per PMGSY guidelines in the rural areas. Rural roads constructed under PMGSY must have proper embankment and drainage. Adequate number and type of Cross Drainage (CD) works, including causeways, where appropriate, must be provided based on site requirements ascertained through necessary investigation. Minor bridges can be provided wherever necessary.

A necessary advisory has been already issued to the State Governments to include the culverts/CDs bridges along with the road proposals.

The proposal of long-span Bridges should be prepared as a separate DPR. However, such proposals of Bridges should be submitted with road proposals in the same batch.

faqs.question: What About Bridges On Rivers/Streams?
faqs.answer:
Bridges on rivers/streams crossing the alignment of the road are taken up under the program along with the road proposal. The Ministry issued PMGSY-III guidelines increasing the span of Long-Span Bridges (LSBs) for funding under PMGSY as follows:

Up to 200 m in respect of Special Category States and LWE districts identified by the MHA.
Upto 150 m in respect of other States.

faqs.question: Whether Compensation For Land Acquisition Is Paid In The Program?
faqs.answer: The rural road is a State subject and it is the responsibility of State Government/ District Panchayat to ensure the availability of land for construction of road works under the programme. In view of the common benefit, generally, the land for construction of roads under PMGSY is made available by the villagers/Panchayat free of cost through voluntary donation. However, in rare cases, if the land is acquired for construction of roads under PMGSY, the State Government is required to pay compensation.

faqs.question: How Are Executants Selected For The Construction Of Roads?
faqs.answer: Executants for construction of roads are selected through open competitive bidding for which well-established procedure for tendering is followed by the State Government. As per provisions, the bidders who have the prescribed qualifications and have the capacity to execute the works are required to take part in the bidding process. To enhance the transparency in tendering and speed up the tendering process, e- procurement of bids has been made mandatory.

faqs.question: If Defects Are Noticed After Completion Of The Road, How Are They Rectified?
faqs.answer: As per provisions of the contract, the contractor is liable for any defect that may occur until 5 years after completion of the road work. To enforce liability of defects, the security amount is deducted from the bills of the contractors. The contractor has to rectify the defect in the above period and if the rectification has not been carried out, the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) is required to rectify the defect and recover the cost from the security deposit of the contractor.

faqs.question: How Is The Quality Of Work Checked And Monitored?
faqs.answer: Every contractor is required to establish a field laboratory in every package of road works in which he/she required to test the quality of material and workmanship under the supervision of executing agency. In addition to checking of quality by departmental officers of executing agency, the State Government is required to deploy independent monitors for monitoring of the quality of road works. Independent National Quality Monitors (NQMs) are also deployed by the Central Government for monitoring the quality of works randomly.

faqs.question: Is There A Provision For The Display Of Project-Related Information At Project Sites?
faqs.answer:
Citizen Information Board in the local language containing the following detailed information of work is provided on each work:-

Description of every layer of work.
Description of the quantity of material involved in work.
How the road will be built and description.
General information board containing information about executing agency, contractor, estimated cost of work and time for completion is also provided on every worksite.

faqs.question: What Is The Role Of Public Representatives In Checking The Quality Of Implementation Of The Programme?
faqs.answer:
In the interest of total transparency and to ensure the pro-active role of public representatives, the States have been advised to organize a time-bound inspection of road works with local public representatives in the following manner:-

The Superintending Engineer would request the Hon'ble M.P. and Zila Pramukh once in 6 months duration to select road works in respective areas and joint inspection/visit would be organized.
The Executive Engineer would request the Hon'ble MLA and Chairperson of Intermediate Panchayat once in three months duration to select road works in respective areas and joint inspection/visit would be organized.
The Assistant Engineer would request the Sarpanch once in two months duration to select road works in respective areas and joint inspection/visit would be organized.

faqs.question: Whether Information About The Programme Is Available On Any Website?
faqs.answer: Yes, information about the programme and details about every work is available on programme website www.omms.nic.in and www.pmgsy.nic.in.The Online Monitoring and Management System (OMMS) is being used for effective management and monitoring under the programme. The required data is entered by the field level staff and the State units under this web-based package.

faqs.question: How Are The Roads Maintained?
faqs.answer: Along with the tendering for the construction the routine maintenance of road works for five years after completion of work is also included. Programme guidelines envisage a transfer of road works for maintenance to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) after 5 years upon completion of the road work.

faqs.question: What Should Be The Population Of Habitations To Be Covered Under PMGSY-I For Providing Connectivity?
faqs.answer: The programme envisages connecting all eligible unconnected habitations by way of an all-weather road as per Core Network with a population of 500 persons (as per 2001 Census) and above in plain areas and 250 persons and above (as per 2001 Census) in the Special Category States (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and Uttarakhand), Tribal (Schedule-V) areas, the Desert Areas (as identified in Desert Development Programme) and in Selected Tribal and Backward Districts (as identified by the Ministry of Home Affairs/Planning Commission). In the critical 267 Left Wing Extremism (LWE) affected blocks (as identified by MHA), additional relaxation has been given to connect habitations with population 100 persons and above (2001 census).

title: CAG Internship Programme
ministry: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
benefits: Selected interns get hands-on experience in government auditing and public finance management. Monthly stipend of ₹10,000 for the duration of internship.
eligibility_summary: Graduate/postgraduate students in Finance, Economics, Law or related disciplines.

title: CAG Research Fellowship
ministry: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
benefits: Annual fellowship of ₹1.5 lakh for research in public auditing methodologies and government accountability.
eligibility_summary: PhD scholars and researchers in public finance, accounting or governance.

title: PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
benefits: ₹6,000 per year in three equal installments of ₹2,000 directly to farmer's bank account.
eligibility_summary: Small and marginal farmer families with combined landholding up to 2 hectares.

title: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
benefits: ₹50,000 per hectare over 3 years for organic farming adoption, certification and marketing support.
eligibility_summary: Farmers willing to adopt organic farming practices and form clusters of 50 acres.

title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
benefits: Insurance coverage for crops at low premium — 2% for Kharif, 1.5% for Rabi. Full actuarial premium covered by Govt for residual losses.
eligibility_summary: All farmers including sharecroppers and tenant farmers growing notified crops.

title: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
benefits: Short-term credit up to ₹3 lakh at 4% interest after 2% interest subvention for prompt repayment. Insurance coverage of ₹50,000 for permanent disability and death.
eligibility_summary: All farmers, sharecroppers, oral lessees and SHG members engaged in crop cultivation.

title: Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA)
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
benefits: Farm schools, demonstrations, exposure visits, and training for farmers. ₹5,000–₹10,000 for participating in technology demonstrations.
eligibility_summary: Small and marginal farmers interested in learning modern agricultural technologies.

title: mKisan Portal – SMS Advisory Services
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
benefits: Free SMS advisory on crop management, weather, market prices, and government schemes in local language.
eligibility_summary: Any farmer with a mobile phone registered on the mKisan portal.

title: National AYUSH Mission (NAM)
ministry: Ministry of Ayush
benefits: Free AYUSH healthcare at PHCs and hospitals. Support for AYUSH practitioners and availability of Ayurvedic, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathic medicines.
eligibility_summary: All citizens seeking AYUSH-based healthcare at government AYUSH facilities.

title: Scholarship Scheme for AYUSH Students (Foreign)
ministry: Ministry of Ayush
benefits: Scholarship for meritorious foreign students pursuing AYUSH courses in Indian institutions. Covers tuition, hostel and monthly stipend.
eligibility_summary: Foreign nationals applying to study AYUSH courses in recognized Indian institutions.

title: Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana – AYUSH Upgradation
ministry: Ministry of Ayush
benefits: Upgradation of district hospitals to include AYUSH wings. Setting up of 12,500 health and wellness centres providing AYUSH services free of cost.
eligibility_summary: Beneficiaries receiving healthcare at upgraded government hospitals across India.

title: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)
ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers
benefits: Quality generic medicines at up to 90% less than branded price at Janaushadhi Kendras. Over 1,900 medicines available.
eligibility_summary: All citizens can purchase medicines at Janaushadhi stores. Storeowners get ₹2.5 lakh startup support.

title: New Urea Policy 2015 – Neem Coated Urea
ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers
benefits: Mandated neem-coating of urea reduces diversion, improves soil health. All urea sold at government-fixed Maximum Retail Price (MRP) with subsidy.
eligibility_summary: Farmers purchasing urea from licensed dealers across India.

title: Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers
benefits: Fixed per-kg subsidy on P&K fertilizers so farmers can access quality fertilizers at affordable prices.
eligibility_summary: Farmers purchasing P&K fertilizers from authorized dealers.

title: Startup India Initiative
ministry: Ministry of Commerce and Industry
benefits: 3-year income tax exemption, 80% rebate on patent fees, self-certification under labour & environmental laws, ₹10,000 crore Fund of Funds.
eligibility_summary: Startups incorporated after April 2016 with annual turnover not exceeding ₹100 crore.

title: Make in India
ministry: Ministry of Commerce and Industry
benefits: Single-window clearances, eased FDI norms, sector-specific incentives for manufacturers. Support for 27 key sectors.
eligibility_summary: Indian and foreign companies looking to set up or expand manufacturing in India.

title: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Commerce and Industry
benefits: 4–6% incentive on incremental sales over base year for 5 years across 14 key sectors including electronics, pharmaceuticals, automobiles.
eligibility_summary: Companies meeting minimum investment thresholds in specified sectors.

title: One District One Product (ODOP) Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Commerce and Industry
benefits: Financial assistance, branding support, and marketing infrastructure for unique products of each district. Micro units get up to ₹10 lakh credit-linked subsidy.
eligibility_summary: Artisans, craftspersons and small producers working with district's identified product.

title: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY)
ministry: Ministry of Communication
benefits: High interest rate (currently 8.2%) savings account for girl child. Tax exemption on deposits, interest and withdrawals under Section 80C.
eligibility_summary: Parents/guardians of girl children below 10 years of age.

title: PM CARES for Children – Post Office Savings
ministry: Ministry of Communication
benefits: Post Office savings accounts with ₹10 lakh corpus at age 18 for children who lost parents to COVID-19. Monthly stipend for schooling and health insurance.
eligibility_summary: Children who lost both parents or legal guardian to COVID-19.

title: National Consumer Helpline (NCH)
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
benefits: Free 24×7 consumer grievance redressal via helpline 1800-11-4000. Online complaint registration and tracking on consumerhelpline.gov.in.
eligibility_summary: Any consumer who has been cheated, received defective goods or unsatisfactory services.

title: IEPF Authority – Unclaimed Dividend Refund
ministry: Ministry of Corporate Affairs
benefits: Recovery of unclaimed dividends and shares transferred to IEPF. No fee for claiming refund.
eligibility_summary: Investors who have unclaimed dividends or shares transferred to IEPF by companies.

title: MCA21 Portal – Easy Business Registration
ministry: Ministry of Corporate Affairs
benefits: Online registration of companies within 24 hours. SPICe+ form integrates PAN, TAN, ESIC, EPFO and bank account opening in single window.
eligibility_summary: Indian citizens and foreign nationals looking to incorporate a company in India.

title: Cultural Talent Search Scholarship Scheme (CTSS)
ministry: Ministry of Culture
benefits: Monthly scholarship of ₹5,000 for 2 years to talented young artists in Indian classical music, dance, theatre, and visual arts.
eligibility_summary: Artists aged 10–14 years showing exceptional talent in traditional performing arts.

title: Senior/Junior Fellowship Scheme for Cultural Studies
ministry: Ministry of Culture
benefits: Junior Fellowship: ₹10,000/month for 2 years. Senior Fellowship: ₹20,000/month for 2 years for outstanding contributions to art, culture, and humanities.
eligibility_summary: Artists, scholars and researchers in Indian culture, heritage, and performing arts.

title: National Cultural Exchange Programme (NCEP)
ministry: Ministry of Culture
benefits: Sponsorship for travel, accommodation and per diem for Indian cultural troupes performing abroad and foreign troupes visiting India.
eligibility_summary: Registered cultural organisations and performing arts groups in India.

title: Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS)
ministry: Ministry of Defence
benefits: Comprehensive medical care at 427+ polyclinics, empanelled private hospitals and government medical colleges for ex-servicemen and dependants.
eligibility_summary: Retired Armed Forces personnel and their dependants.

title: Agniveer Seva Nidhi Package
ministry: Ministry of Defence
benefits: Agniveers receive ₹11.71 lakh tax-free Seva Nidhi package at exit. Additional ₹48 lakh life insurance for death in harness, re-employment priority in CAPFs.
eligibility_summary: Youth aged 17.5–23 years enrolled under the Agnipath scheme.

title: Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme for Ex-Servicemen
ministry: Ministry of Defence
benefits: Scholarship of ₹2,500/month for boys and ₹3,000/month for girls pursuing professional degree courses. Priority for wards of ex-servicemen killed/disabled in action.
eligibility_summary: Wards/widows of ex-servicemen and coast guard personnel for professional education.

title: PM-DevINE – PM Development Initiative for NE Region
ministry: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region
benefits: ₹6,600 crore outlay for social development, livelihood support, infrastructure and industry in 8 North-Eastern states.
eligibility_summary: Residents of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura.
